# Markdown {.subsection background-color="#425556"}

## Markdown is a *simple* "markup" language

::: {.content-box-marine}
A markup language allows you to format a document with **commands** instead of menu items.
:::

For instance, you can:

::: {.incremental}
-   Enclose a word between two sets of \*\*two asterisks\*\* to obtain **bold text**.

-   Enclose a word between \_underscores\_ to produce *italic text*.

-   Create headers and subheaders at various levels with `#`, `##` and `###`.

> -   Define a quote block by placing `>` in front of the quote.
:::



## Markdown can be rendered in various formats

-   `html`

-   `pdf`

-   MS Word

# R Markdown {.subsection background-color="#425556"}

## R Markdown {.smaller}

::: {.content-box-marine}
R Markdown combines **text written with Markdown** and **code written with R**.
:::

This is useful in two ways:

::: {.fragment}
-   **As a tool for analysis**:

    -   R Markdown **replaces scripts** when carrying out analyses.

    -   You can **execute the R code** contained in the R Markdown document to analyse your data.

    -   Since it allows for text, it can be used to **document your data analysis**.
:::

::: {.fragment}
-   **As a reporting tool**:

    -   It can produce reports in various formats, including `.pdf`, `.docx` and `html`.

    -   Rendering in `html` allows for some degree of **interactivity**.
:::

# Quarto {.subsection background-color="#425556"}

## Quarto is the **next-generation version of R Markdown** {.smaller}


-   It is designed to work with **multiple languages**, across **multiple platforms** and **IDEs**.

    -   Languages supported: **R, Python, Julia, Observable**.

    -   IDEs: **RStudio, Jupyter Notebooks, VS Code, NeoVim**.

-   It **works seamlessly with R**, since it is developed by Posit PBC (the company behind the RStudio IDE).

-   Recent versions of the RStudio IDE provide a **Visual Quarto Editor**.

    -   This makes things easier, as **there's no need to know all the Markdown commands!**

::: callout-note
The notebooks in this workshop are written in **Quarto**.
:::

# Your first notebook {.subsection background-color="#425556"}

## Create a new document

::: panel-tabset
### R Markdown

-   `File` → `New File` → `R Markdown...`

### Quarto

-   `File` → `New File` → `Quarto Document...`
:::

The default choice for new documents is HTML.

::: {.callout-important icon="false"}
## Exercise

To follow the next sections, create your own R Markdown / Quarto document!
:::

## YAML options {.smaller}

Look closely at the header of the template.

-   In any Quarto/R Markdown document, there's a *header* written in YAML.

-   In the header, we provide the rendering options, for instance the basic document information:

::: panel-tabset
### R Markdown

``` yaml
title: "Working with R Markdown"
author: MYSELF
output: html_document
```

### Quarto

``` yaml
title: "Working with Quarto"
author: MYSELF
format: html
editor: visual
```

In Quarto, you can also choose which editor you want to use!
:::

The YAML header can be populated with many options.

::: callout-note
We will discuss these options at the end of the workshop.
:::

## Insert a code chunk {.smaller}

-   Code is written in *chunks*. To insert one:

    -   use the <kbd>+C</kbd> button at the top of the script editor,

    -   or the shortcut <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>I</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Option</kbd> + <kbd>I</kbd> on a Mac).

-   An empty chunk looks like this:

```` markdown
```{{r}}

```
````

-   Inside, you can write some R code. For instance, the object `cars` contains data on the speed and the stopping distance of cars:

```` markdown
```{{r}}
cars
```
````

## Execute a code chunk {.smaller}

-  Use the *play* button ▶️ on its right-hand side,

-  Or the shortcut <kbd>Ctrl/Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Enter</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd</kbd>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r cars}
cars
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r plot-cars}
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of the cars data: stopping distance increases with speed."
plot(cars)
```
:::
::::

## *Knitting*, or the art of *rendering* a document {.smaller}

Once you're done with your analysis, click on the `Knit` / `Render` button at the top of the source editor to produce a document.


## Exercise

Time to get your fingers dirty!

In your newly created R Markdown / Quarto document:

-   **Modify the YAML header**: add a title, an author and a date.

-   **Write some text**, e.g. add a header and a short sentence.

-   **Insert a chunk**:

    -   Add a couple of simple commands, e.g. compute `5 + 5` and `30 / 6`.

    -   Execute the chunk with the **play button** or the shortcut.

-   Save the file in a convenient location, then *Knit* / *Render* it.
